For a harmonic function \(v\) on the unit ball, the restriction of \(v\) to the sphere \(\partial B\) is a real‑analytic function (a finite linear combination of spherical harmonics).  
If a non‑zero analytic function on the sphere vanishes together with all its first‑order partial derivatives at a point, then by the analyticity the vanishing set cannot contain any open piece of the sphere; otherwise the function would be identically zero (by analytic continuation). Consequently the set  

\[
Z(v)=\{x\in\partial B : v(x)=\partial_{x_1}v(x)=\partial_{x_2}v(x)=\partial_{x_3}v(x)=0\}
\]

consists only of isolated points.  An isolated set has zero \(2\)-dimensional Hausdorff (surface‑area) measure. Hence for every admissible non‑zero \(v\),

\[
\int_{Z(v)} dS = 0 .
\]

Since the value is always zero, the supremum over all such functions is also zero.
